requirements: Verify source head and ownership. Use an isolated clean checkout, unoccupied fixed ports, the host's bounded runtime wrapper and periodic heartbeat. Use a different fixed port consistently if required.

For fail-before, replace only solr/bin/solr with the exact contributor head version, keeping the new test and JVM marker code intact. This is a synthetic shell-only mutation, not an entirely unmodified contributor build. The focused marker ordering assertion must fail with two running nodes; startup, compilation, timeout or skipped tests are not valid negative proof. Retain logs and XML.

Restore the exact source head before positive runs. Run both packaging test variants, tidy and root check with the normal security manager. Record fresh logs/XML and actual commands, exit codes, skips and timeouts. Tidy must leave no changes; a repair requires a new source head and gate.

The test masks the JVM flag from the classification command and forces PID discovery order while using real Solr processes; it does not prove environment-only startup or every alternate configuration. No macOS result is claimed. No code or test authoring is assigned to the gate worker.
The older failed Linux run was owner-stopped after a hung HTTP call; ensure cleanup of all spawned processes and apply the host time limit. Do not repeat an unbounded test.
